name: Monique Appeaning
current_role: Former Baton Rouge assistant chief administrative officer
bio: Monique Appeaning is a former assistant chief administrative officer for the City of Baton Rouge and a former budget analyst for the Louisiana National Guard, and she reports more than 25 years in public service. She holds bachelor's and master's degrees in public administration from Southern University, ran for the Louisiana House in 2023, and founded the St. George Republican Women's Club.

platform.point: Back law enforcement, fight violent crime and trafficking, and modernize the military.
Cut taxes for working Americans and end taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security.
Reduce government waste.
Rebuild domestic manufacturing and support Louisiana agriculture and small businesses.
Pursue full American energy independence.
Lower prescription drug and health care costs for seniors and address Medicare and Social Security concerns.
Expand apprenticeships and job training and strengthen universities.
Hold a visible presence across all parishes in the district and pursue congressional oversight.

economy.evidence: Calls for tax cuts, no tax on tips, overtime or Social Security, and less government waste.

liberty.evidence: Describes herself as pro-life (abortion) and pro-Second Amendment (guns).

security.evidence: Campaign pledges to back law enforcement and combat violent crime and trafficking.

energy.evidence: General statement: her campaign site calls for full American energy independence, without a specific policy.

notes: Searched the campaign site (its issues and about subpages return 404), Talk 107.3, WRKF, Central City News and race roundups; she has raised carbon capture and property rights concerns without stating a policy. No statements were found on immigration, foreign policy, technology, schools, faith or welfare programs.

name: Larry Davis III
current_role: Minister and Livingston Parish Republican Executive Committee member
bio: Larry Davis III is a lifelong Livingston Parish resident from Denham Springs, a licensed minister and a member of the Livingston Parish Republican Executive Committee who describes himself as a middle-class worker. He first ran in Louisiana's 5th District and moved his campaign to the 6th District in February 2026.

platform.point: Lower costs through reduced federal spending, deregulation, pro-job tax policy and domestic energy production.
Build physical barriers where needed, crack down on cartels, require employment verification and close asylum loopholes.
Support police, raise penalties for violent crime and target human trafficking and fentanyl distribution.
Protect parental rights and curriculum transparency, reject federal mandates and expand school choice.
Increase domestic drilling and refining, support nuclear power and oppose carbon capture projects he says harm residents.
Defend First and Second Amendment rights and oppose surveillance expansion, digital IDs and a central bank digital currency.
Set government AI guardrails, block data sales to adversaries and shield children from harmful algorithms.
Require voter ID, maintain clean voter rolls, restrict ballot harvesting and adopt congressional term limits.

economy.evidence: Campaign platform calls for reduced federal spending, deregulation, pro-job tax initiatives and balanced budgets.

welfare.evidence: General statement: seeks lower health costs through insurance competition, pricing transparency and limits on pharmacy middlemen rather than new public programs.

liberty.evidence: Says life begins at conception and backs traditional marriage (abortion, LGBTQ), but defends gun rights, opposes federal censorship and supports vaccine choice (guns, speech).

security.evidence: Backs police and tougher penalties for violent crime but opposes expanded surveillance and digital ID systems.

immigration.evidence: Supports physical border barriers, mandatory employment verification and closing asylum loopholes.

energy.evidence: Calls for more domestic drilling and refining and fewer regulatory barriers for producers, and opposes carbon capture projects.

tech.evidence: Supports government AI guardrails and protecting children from harmful algorithms while favoring market-driven innovation.

education.evidence: Backs parental rights, curriculum transparency, local control and expanded school choice.

faith.evidence: General statement: as a licensed minister he says public policy should reflect biblical values, without naming a specific policy.

notes: Used the campaign site's policies page, a KALB interview and race roundups; the Livingston Parish News and Louisiana Illuminator pages blocked automated access. His military plan covers readiness and veterans but says nothing on alliances or foreign aid, so foreign policy stays unknown.

name: Michael Mebruer
bio: Michael Mebruer is a traveling medical professional from St. Francisville in West Feliciana Parish and an LSU economics graduate who reports graduate study in financial economics. He has not held public office before, first entered the 5th District race and now runs in the 6th District after the 2026 redistricting, with a self-funded campaign that takes no donations.

platform.point: Tackle trillion-dollar deficits through structural reform of major spending drivers and a smaller federal bureaucracy.
Shift Medicare toward competing private plans that give seniors more choice while keeping beneficiary protections.
Give states more Medicaid flexibility and widen private insurance options for low-income Americans.
Simplify the tax code and remove special provisions that benefit well-connected interests.
Make E-Verify mandatory, penalize employers who hire unauthorized workers and strengthen border enforcement.
Describes himself as pro-life.

economy.evidence: Calls for simpler taxes that do not punish success, structural spending reform and a smaller federal bureaucracy.

welfare.evidence: Proposes restructuring entitlements, moving Medicare toward competing private plans and giving states Medicaid flexibility.

liberty.evidence: General statement: says he defends the protection of innocent human life (abortion); no stated views on other liberty issues.

immigration.evidence: Supports mandatory E-Verify, meaningful penalties for employers of unauthorized workers and stronger border enforcement.

notes: His campaign site and X handle spell the name Mebruer, while WBRZ and the Louisiana Illuminator use Mebreur; the ballot spelling is unconfirmed. Searched his site and qualifying coverage; a Livingston Parish News debate report was blocked, and no statements were found on policing, foreign policy, energy, technology, schools or faith.

name: Richard E. Neal
bio: Richard Neal has served in the U.S. House since 1989, representing Massachusetts's 1st District since 2013, and is ranking member of the Ways and Means Committee, which he chaired from 2019 to 2023. Raised in Springfield, he served on the Springfield City Council and as mayor of Springfield from 1983 to 1989.

platform.point: Favors middle-class tax cuts over tax cuts for the wealthy.
Wants tariffs removed to bring down consumer prices.
Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare.
Aims to lower health care and prescription drug costs.
Points to his role leading the Inflation Reduction Act's climate and clean-energy tax credits through Ways and Means.
Supports comprehensive reform with a path to citizenship for Dreamers and undocumented immigrants, and backs birthright citizenship.
Backs an assault weapons ban, universal background checks and a minimum purchase age of 21.
Seeks federal resources for Western and Central Massachusetts.

economy.evidence: Opposes tax cuts for the wealthy and tariffs and seeks to close high-earner loopholes.

welfare.evidence: Helped write the ACA but opposed Medicare for All in favor of incremental reform.

liberty.evidence: Mixed abortion record (voted for the 2003 partial-birth ban, cosponsored the Women's Health Protection Act), opposed the Federal Marriage Amendment (LGBTQ), and backs an assault weapons ban and universal background checks (guns).

immigration.evidence: Campaign site backs a path to citizenship for Dreamers and undocumented immigrants, birthright citizenship and expanded work visas.

foreign.evidence: Opposed a July 2026 amendment cutting Israel aid and backs Iron Dome funding with aid conditions, but opposed the July 2026 House NDAA over its $1 trillion total and criticizes reckless wars.

energy.evidence: Led the Inflation Reduction Act's $370 billion climate and clean-energy package through Ways and Means and calls climate action urgent.

education.evidence: Promotes the American Rescue Plan's $130 billion for K-12 schools and federal education earmarks for his district.

notes: Read the campaign issue pages (environment, immigration, gun violence) and House press releases on Israel aid, the NDAA and school funding. No clear record was found on surveillance, tech regulation beyond an IRS AI pilot markup, or religion in public life.

name: Bill Keating
bio: Bill Keating has served in the U.S. House since 2011 and represents the South Coast, South Shore, Cape Cod and Islands district. He previously served in the Massachusetts House and Senate and was Norfolk County District Attorney from 1999 to 2011. He sits on the Armed Services and Foreign Affairs committees and is ranking member of the Europe subcommittee.

platform.point: Lead on European security and support for Ukraine through the Foreign Affairs Europe subcommittee.
Close the loophole that lets people on FBI watchlists buy firearms.
Back unions, collective bargaining, fair wages and workplace safety.
Expand solar and wind, extend tax incentives to offshore renewables and end subsidies for major oil companies.
Move spent nuclear fuel into dry cask storage and press for oversight of the Pilgrim plant's decommissioning.
Demand due process in immigration arrests and oppose enforcement that separates families with pending asylum claims.
Treat access to high-quality, affordable health care as a basic right and defend Social Security and Medicare.
Support strong federal funding for education programs.

economy.evidence: Wants to end subsidies for major oil companies, backs direct federal investment in regional industries and supports union bargaining rights.

welfare.evidence: General statement: calls affordable, high-quality health care a basic human right and opposes Social Security and Medicare cuts.

liberty.evidence: Votes for abortion rights, backed ending Don't Ask, Don't Tell (LGBTQ) and supports tighter gun purchase rules.

immigration.evidence: Criticized a 2026 ICE arrest in his district as cruelty-first enforcement and urged due process, family reunification and faster asylum decisions.

foreign.evidence: Ranking member of the Europe subcommittee and active in the Ukraine Caucus.

energy.evidence: Supports federal incentives for solar and offshore wind, ending oil company subsidies and reducing fossil fuel reliance to address climate change.

education.evidence: General statement: his House issues page backs robust federal funding for education programs.

faith.evidence: Cosponsored the Equitable Access to Care and Health Act creating religious exemptions under the ACA.

notes: Found the campaign site keatingforcongress.com (no issues page) and used his House issue pages and statements. Security is left null because his record mixes law-enforcement support as a former DA with privacy bills; no tech regulation record was found, and the faith score rests on a single cosponsorship.

name: Tyler MacAllister
current_role: Former Mattapoisett Select Board chair and charter fishing captain
bio: Tyler MacAllister is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 9th district and a charter boat captain who has fished local waters for more than 40 years. He has lived in Mattapoisett since 2001 and served five terms on its Select Board, finishing as chair in April 2026. He reports a business master's degree and a marine biology degree and appeared on the TV series Harpoon Hunters.

platform.point: Protect the fishing fleet and waterfront with science-based policy and fewer federal rules that burden fishermen.
Bring down grocery, fuel and housing costs by challenging mandates and federal spending.
Take an all-of-the-above approach that puts affordable, reliable power first.
Oppose industrial wind farms in fishing grounds and data centers that strain the power grid and water supply.
Support local police and common-sense child-safety standards.
Cut waste and excess spending in Washington.
Honor commitments to veterans and protect seniors' earned benefits.
Promote domestic seafood, including bluefin tuna, noting the U.S. imports most of its seafood.

economy.evidence: General statement: wants to cut federal waste and challenge mandates and Washington spending he links to higher costs.

security.evidence: General statement: lists support for local police and community safety as a priority.

energy.evidence: Backs all-of-the-above energy focused on affordability and opposes offshore wind farms in fishing grounds such as Vineyard Wind.

notes: His campaign site spells the surname Macallister. Searched the site's home, solutions and about pages plus Sippican Week and Boston Broadside coverage; no statements were found on immigration, abortion, guns, health care, foreign policy, technology, schools or faith.

name: John Deaton
bio: John Deaton is an attorney known for asbestos litigation and cryptocurrency cases who founded the Deaton Law Firm in Rhode Island in 2006 and served in the Marine Corps as a judge advocate. He was the 2024 Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Massachusetts and won the unopposed 2026 Republican primary to face Senator Ed Markey.

platform.point: Set federal AI rules with a three-year safe harbor, disclosure for high-risk models and limits on non-consensual training imagery.
Impose strict federal limits on license-plate cameras, including court orders for historical searches and rapid data purges.
Raise the payroll tax cap and gradually raise the retirement age for future workers only.
Reject both blanket amnesty and mass deportation, secure the border and offer DACA recipients an earned path to citizenship.
Break up vertically integrated insurers, curb pharmacy benefit manager practices and create a national telehealth license compact.
Build five million homes in five years through zoning reform and fewer construction barriers.
Oppose the Green New Deal, pursue an all-of-the-above transition including nuclear, and amend the Jones Act for LNG shipping.
Support abortion rights and disagree with the Dobbs decision.

economy.evidence: Proposes raising the Social Security payroll tax cap and antitrust breakups of large insurers, alongside zoning and construction deregulation.

welfare.evidence: Defends Social Security but would raise the retirement age for future workers, prefers market-based health reforms and puts universal basic income on the table for AI job loss.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights, same-sex marriage and Massachusetts's existing gun laws (abortion, LGBTQ, guns).

security.evidence: Wants strict federal limits on license-plate camera networks, including court orders for historical searches and a ban on warrantless queries.

immigration.evidence: Rejects mass deportation and blanket amnesty, backs an earned citizenship path for DACA recipients, border security and more legal immigration.

foreign.evidence: Says foreign aid must clearly serve U.S. interests and criticizes blank checks and large non-military aid spending abroad.

energy.evidence: Opposes the Green New Deal and a net-zero-by-2050 target but backs an all-of-the-above transition with solar, wind and nuclear.

tech.evidence: Proposes federal AI rules with a three-year safe harbor and disclosure for high-risk models, prefers voluntary provenance standards, and opposes Warren-style crypto regulation.

notes: Found the 2026 campaign site and used its issues page; the Axios profile blocked access and no headshot URL was identified. His education plans cover student loans and trade training, which do not fit the school-choice scale, and no statements on religion in public life were found.

name: Berney Flowers
bio: Berney Flowers is a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel from Elkridge who served nearly 21 years, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, and later worked in Defense Department cybersecurity roles including the launch of U.S. Cyber Command. He holds a Harvard cybersecurity certificate, was appointed to a Maryland judicial nominating commission in 2021, and won the 2026 Republican nomination in Maryland's 3rd District.

platform.point: Impose budget caps and fiscal discipline, cutting with a scalpel rather than a sledgehammer.
Cut taxes so working families keep more of what they earn.
Pursue strong immigration enforcement that puts national safety first.
Treat the right to bear arms as non-negotiable and oppose limits on law-abiding owners.
Expand domestic energy production to reduce reliance on foreign oil.
Protect the Bay through practical, locally informed measures rather than heavy regulation.
Track federal rebuilding funds transparently to avoid bureaucratic delays.
Depoliticize public schools and promote parental involvement and local control.

economy.evidence: Supports binding budget caps and tax cuts and says the federal government spends too much.

liberty.evidence: Calls the right to bear arms non-negotiable and opposes restrictions on law-abiding gun owners (guns only).

security.evidence: General statement: pledges resources and respect for police and stronger security policies.

immigration.evidence: General statement: calls for strong immigration enforcement and border defense.

energy.evidence: General statement: wants to unleash domestic energy production and opposes burdensome Bay regulation.

education.evidence: General statement: backs parental involvement and local control while calling for depoliticized public schools.

notes: Found the campaign site flowersformaryland.com and used its home and about pages plus the Baltimore Sun questionnaire; Vote Smart and Ballotpedia were not used. No statements were found on health care or safety-net programs, abortion, foreign policy, technology regulation or faith.
